subject: language
intro: I'm Mr. Brooks, 7th grade ELA. Let's plan an argument writing lesson on claims and evidence.

beats.narration: The title makes it feel like a debate, which is exactly the energy I want.
This standard asks students to write arguments supporting claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.
Claim plus reasons plus evidence is the basic structure.
beats.text: Students will be able to write a clear claim and support it with two reasons and relevant evidence.

beats.narration: Physically taking a side makes the claim concrete.
beats.text: Four corners: "Should school start later?" Students move to Strongly Agree, Agree, Disagree, or Strongly Disagree and share one reason.

beats.narration: The weak vs. strong comparison is the key teaching point.
beats.text: Model the difference between a claim, a reason, and evidence using the school start topic. Show weak vs. strong evidence (opinion vs. statistic).

beats.narration: Reading articles gives them real evidence to use.
beats.text: Students read two short articles on the topic and complete a claim-reasons-evidence organizer, then write a body paragraph.

beats.narration: A focused check on the core structure.
beats.text: Write your claim and one reason with evidence from the articles.

outro: Debate, model, research, write. Now it's your turn.
